elements.text: Every time I use the quantile function I really feel it needs to use the names provided to the
probs
argument. So I can do
quantile(x, probs = c(low = 0.05, mid = 0.5, high = 0.95))
or similar. It should be a relatively straightforward addition, something like this:
Would this be a good topic for r-dev you think?

text:
Keep in mind that `quantile` is a generic. The implementation of `stats:::quantile.default` looks like it has an opportunity for replacing the names where they're currently set with `names(qs) <- format_perc(probs, digits = digits)` .

I'd consider an even broader improvement of retaining the probs either way, perhaps as an attribute - they can currently be recovered with some string manipulation, but consider

```R> quantile(runif(5), probs = c(1/3, 2/3))
33.33333% 66.66667%
0.3384649 0.5921896```
Particularly if you replaced these with arbitrary names, it would be impossible to recover what values were used (aside from the source).

Attributes other than `names` are currently printed, and I doubt a proposal to make a new structure would go anywhere, so for a minimal prototype I used `comment` which doesn't print, but does require a character string, whereas a `language` object itself from `substitute` might not be a bad thing

```quantile2 <- function(x, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) {
  res <- quantile(x, probs)
  comment(res) <- deparse(substitute(probs))
  if (!is.null(names(probs))) {
    setNames(res, names(probs))
  } else {
    res
  }
}

vals <- runif(50)

x <- quantile2(vals, probs = c(1/3, 2/3))
x
#> 33.33333% 66.66667%
#> 0.4329540 0.6776829
comment(x)
#> [1] "c(1/3, 2/3)"

y <- quantile2(vals)
y
#>         0%        25%        50%        75%       100%
#> 0.01259037 0.32146006 0.53364646 0.82721406 0.99776432
comment(y)
#> [1] "seq(0, 1, 0.25)"

z <- quantile2(vals, probs = c(low = 1/3, hi = 2/3))
z
#>       low        hi
#> 0.4329540 0.6776829
comment(z)
#> [1] "c(low = 1/3, hi = 2/3)"```
This still may not be ideal, as passing in variables doesn't resolve to the values, e.g. `probs = c(lo, hi)`.

text:
I guess I never though about having to recover the underlying probabilities. That's also a good improvement.

quantile.default has access to the numerical values of the probabilities, so deparse(substitude()) might not be needed if we solve this in quantile.default directly.
